title: 2020 roadmap on pore materials for energy and environmental applications
claim: Self-supporting metallic aerogels can avoid carbon-support corrosion and particle detachment while retaining accessible, interconnected catalytic backbones.
explanation: The review contrasts metal aerogels with conventional catalyst nanoparticles on carbon black, whose support can corrode during high-potential fuel-cell events.
scope: Unsupported metallic aerogel electrocatalysts for fuel-cell reactions.
conditions: High-potential start-up, shut-down, or local fuel-starvation events are cited as conditions under which carbon-support durability matters.
caveats: Avoiding a carbon support does not establish immunity from other degradation mechanisms or practical durability.
